claim.pdf_says: Page 391 opens with a stand-alone hanging paragraph, indented to the level of the a)/b)/c) sub-item text of syntax rule 14) which ends on page 390: 'where length is the length of the literal as specified in 8.3.3, Literals.'  Page 390's sub-item c) ends at "If the literal is national, 'PICTURE N(length)'" with no trailing text (verified at 300 dpi).
claim.markdown_says: The page-391 slice begins directly at '15) If BLANK WHEN ZERO or JUSTIFIED is specified, a COLUMN clause shall also be specified.' The sentence instead appears glued onto page 390's sub-item c):  "c) If the literal is national, 'PICTURE N(length)' where length is the length of the literal as specified in 8.3.3, Literals."
claim.why_it_matters: In the PDF the paragraph is a hanging qualifier for ALL THREE implied-PICTURE cases a) X(length), b) 1(length) and c) N(length); merged into c) it reads as defining 'length' only for the national case, leaving the alphanumeric and boolean cases with an undefined 'length'. It also mis-attributes page-391 text to page 390, so a page-anchored citation to this sentence lands on the wrong page. Note the same sentence is transcribed correctly as a stand-alone paragraph elsewhere in the file (two other occurrences), so this is a local regression, not a house style.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED independently, at 300 dpi, on both pages, with pixel geometry rather than eyeballing.

(1) PDF p390 (printed 360, verso): syntax rule 14)'s sub-item c) is the LAST body line on the page. Its dark-pixel runs are (340-369)='c)', (413-670)='If the', (686-846)='literal', (862-1244)="is national, 'PICTURE N(length)'". Rightmost ink on that band is x=1244; the next non-blank band on the page is y=3111 = the footer '360 (c)ISO/IEC 2023'. So c) genuinely ends at "'PICTURE N(length)'" with NO trailing text. The claim does not misquote the PDF here.

(2) PDF p391 (printed 361, recto): the first body band, y=388-429, is a single unbroken run x=407-1690 reading exactly 'where length is the length of the literal as specified in 8.3.3, Literals.' The next band, y=494-534, is '15) If BLANK WHEN ZERO...'. The vertical gap (429->494 = 65 px) is identical to every other inter-paragraph gap on both pages (e.g. 534->599 = 65, rule-14 body 2589 -> a) 2654 = 65). It is therefore a normal sibling PARAGRAPH, not a wrapped continuation line and not page-break furniture.

(3) Refutation angle 'text is merely reflowed / only page-break furniture' FAILS. The paragraph does not begin on page 390 and spill onto 391 -- it begins and ends wholly on 391, while c) is complete on 390. So the markdown is not applying a defensible 'keep a spanning paragraph with the page it starts on' convention; it moved a wholly-page-391 paragraph backwards onto page 390 AND fused it into a different block (sub-item c)) rather than emitting it as its own paragraph. Two separate defects in one edit.

(4) Refutation angle 'no change in meaning' FAILS on scope. Measured indents prove the scoping. p390 is a verso and p391 a recto with mirrored margins, so the whole p391 text block is shifted +71 px (rule-label column 267 -> 338); columns must be compared inside each page's own frame. p390 frame: rule-label col 269, rule-body/continuation col 340, a)/b)/c) LABEL col 339-340, sub-item TEXT col 413. p391 frame: rule-label col 338, rule-body col 408. The 'where length' line sits at x=407, i.e. 336 after de-shifting = the rule-14 BODY / sub-item-label column. The sub-item TEXT column would be 413+71 = 484, and it is not there. So the sentence is set one indent level OUTDENTED from a)/b)/c)'s text, at the level that closes rule 14) as a whole -- unambiguously qualifying all three implied PICTUREs. Fusing it into c) demotes a normative definition that governs X(length), 1(length) and N(length) into a relative clause governing N(length) alone.

(5) The claimed local-regression framing checks out and is corroborating, not decorative. The file's other two transcriptions of the same sentence are both stand-alone paragraphs set at the SAME indent as their a) label -- ISO_COBOL.md:16953 (page 395, three-space indent matching '   a) if the literal is alphanumeric') and ISO_COBOL.md:17251 (page 401, flush-left matching flush-left 'a)'). Both of those passages fall entirely inside one PDF page, i.e. no page boundary to trip over; the defective one at ISO_COBOL.md:16769 is precisely the instance where the paragraph landed across a page break. That both matches the PDF geometry I measured and identifies the mechanism.

One inaccuracy in the claim's wording (corrected below): the indent level is misstated. The paragraph is at the a)/b)/c) LABEL / rule-body column, not at the sub-item TEXT column. That correction strengthens rather than weakens the finding -- rule-body level is exactly the level that scopes the sentence to the entire rule. Also, no text is LOST: every word is present in the markdown, so this is purely a re-scoping plus page mis-attribution, not an omission.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, with two corrections to the description.

What is actually wrong: the sentence 'where length is the length of the literal as specified in 8.3.3, Literals.' is a stand-alone paragraph whose sole location in the PDF is the first body line of page 391 (printed 361), closing syntax rule 14) of 13.15.3. ISO_COBOL.md instead appends it to the end of sub-item c) inside the page-390 slice (ISO_COBOL.md:16769), so the page-391 slice opens at '15) If BLANK WHEN ZERO...'. Two defects: the paragraph break is lost (fused into c)), and the content is attributed to page 390 instead of 391.

Correction 1 -- indent level. The claim says the paragraph is 'indented to the level of the a)/b)/c) sub-item text'. It is not. Measured at 300 dpi and de-shifted for the recto/verso mirrored margin (+71 px on p391), it sits at x=407 = the a)/b)/c) LABEL column (340 in p390's frame), which is also rule 14)'s own body/continuation column. The sub-item text column would be 484 on p391. The paragraph is thus one level OUTDENTED from a)/b)/c)'s text, at the level that terminates rule 14) as a whole -- which is precisely why it governs all three implied PICTUREs. The file's own two correct transcriptions (ISO_COBOL.md:16953 on page 395, ISO_COBOL.md:17251 on page 401) place it at exactly that indent, level with their a) label, confirming both the geometry and the intended house style.

Correction 2 -- nothing is missing. Every word is present in the markdown. This is a scoping and page-attribution defect, not an omission: the normative definition of 'length' is demoted from qualifying a) X(length), b) 1(length) and c) N(length) to qualifying only c) N(length), and a page-anchored citation to it resolves to page-390 instead of page-391.

Correct fix: delete " where length is the length of the literal as specified in 8.3.3, Literals." from ISO_COBOL.md:16769 so c) ends at "'PICTURE N(length)'", and emit the sentence as its own paragraph at the top of the page-391 slice, indented three spaces to match the '   a)' / '   b)' / '   c)' labels above it -- i.e. the same shape already used at ISO_COBOL.md:16953.
